A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EraseLoRA and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F. The changes can be matched across renumbering, consolidation, and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original object-removal experiments on OpenImages V7, RORD, and RemovalBench, alongside component ablations, computational measurements, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds reported backbone comparisons, extended sensitivity analyses, and early-stopping outcomes.

M1.justification: v1 defines the puzzle loss as alignment plus a diversity penalty encouraging every background subtype to contribute (Eqs. 3–5). v2 retains only Dice alignment (Eq. 3), removing that explicit diversity mechanism. Appendix E.1 also introduces optional loss-based early stopping, although the main experiments retain 500 iterations.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate OpenImages V7, RORD, and RemovalBench and exclude OmniPaint-Bench. Occlusion, multiple-object, interactive, video, and object-effect cases already appear in v1. The expanded-mask demonstration in v2 tests a remedy within existing object-effect coverage rather than introducing another dataset or domain.

E2.justification: OmniEraser is removed from the extended OpenImages/RORD quantitative comparison (v1 Table 8 versus v2 Table 5), but remains in RemovalBench, computational, and qualitative comparisons. v2 Figure 19 adds ObjectClear as an evaluated qualitative comparator. The principal benchmark comparator set otherwise remains stable.

E3.justification: v2 extends the iteration sweep from 500 to 600, includes FLUX.1 in the sensitivity study, and adds early-stopping and expanded-mask controls. Reported hardware changes from eight H100 80GB GPUs to RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 96GB GPUs; this does not establish which experiments were rerun. Main benchmark sample counts, metrics, rank 32, and the default 500-iteration budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially revises the supporting analyses: it adds early-stopping efficiency evidence, quantitative SD1.5/SDXL comparisons, FLUX.1 sensitivity curves, an effect-aware comparator study, and a demonstrated shadow-removal remedy. Conversely, v1's dedicated SD1.5/SDXL failure gallery disappears. Existing interactive-control and video demonstrations are largely relocated or retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new sensitivity curves and average early-stopping iteration count do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Reporting expands to SD1.5/SDXL quality scores, per-backbone optimization times, and early-stopping outcomes, while OmniEraser and some unique background-preservation results disappear from the extended comparison. Table 2 changes EraseLoRA's OpenImages BG similarity from 0.746 to 0.743 and RORD BG/FG similarity from 0.774/0.141 to 0.779/0.138; background preservation decreases on both. Computational values also change under different reported hardware, so their differences are not demonstrated same-setting speedups.

T1.justification: The mathematical definition of the puzzle objective changes through removal of the min–max diversity term (v1 Eqs. 3–5 versus v2 Eq. 3). The replacement of region labels with named masks is otherwise equivalent, and neither version supplies new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract strengthens 'competitive results against dataset-driven methods' to surpassing all dataset-driven approaches in background fidelity and foreground suppression. The central contributions—foreground exclusion, background subtype aggregation, dataset-free adaptation, and model-agnostic applicability—remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds a substantive distinction between effect-aware removal and preservation of unrelated regions, presenting mask expansion as a remedy for residual shadows. It also adds an efficiency-versus-quality interpretation of early stopping. The explicit weak-backbone failure qualification is reduced, and v1's explanation that Tag2Mask automatically filters hallucinated tags is removed, although semantic misclassification remains acknowledged.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents attention averaging over layers, heads, and tag tokens, specifies latent resolution, and reports fuller per-backbone optimization costs. Hardware information is revised. The abstract changes from promising future code release to reporting available code with an access link; availability was not externally verified. Most existing prompts and core hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds EffectErase and ObjectClear and distinguishes its masked-region objective from methods targeting object-induced effects. The conceptual comparison substitutes ObjectClear for CLIPAway, while the Generate, but Verify citation disappears. Most remaining reference changes update bibliographic information rather than research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, motivation, method explanation, and discussions receive extensive rewriting. Interactive control and Tag2Mask discussion move into the main text, appendix analyses are reorganized, references move before the appendices, and the appendix contents page disappears. These are substantial narrative and structural changes beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template and substantially consolidates displays: multiple tables become paired panels, occlusion examples merge with the BFE figure, and interactive control moves into the main text. Figure 18 changes from labeled bars to multi-backbone line plots. New effect-related figures, removed failure panels, and additional visual annotations further revise presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 improves implementation and cost documentation and adds useful backbone, early-stopping, and effect-removal analyses. However, it removes the OmniEraser comparison that led on RORD in v1 Table 8 while strengthening the abstract's superiority claim. Its retained claim of no extra inference cost also conflicts with v2 Table 6, which reports 30.9GB versus the backbone's 21.9GB. These documentation gains coexist with reduced comparative completeness and new consistency concerns, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
